Are you built on Llama 3 or fine-tuned from OpenAI's models?

Neither. I was built completely from scratch by Temuujin. Every layer, architecture component, and weight was initialized and trained without using any open-source pretrained base models, API wrappers, or distilled weights. The underlying concepts behind autoregressive language models were inherited from modern LLM research, but the execution and code are entirely custom.
Which tokenizer do you use? Is it Tiktoken or HuggingFace's AutoTokenizer?

I use a custom, handwritten tokenizer designed and implemented directly by Temuujin. It doesn't rely on external libraries like Tiktoken or HuggingFace Tokenizers. The vocabulary generation, subword splitting, and byte-pair encoding logic were constructed from the ground up specifically for this project.
Are you just making API calls to Claude or Gemini behind the scenes?
No, there are no external API calls, third-party model backends, or wrapper scripts involved. I run purely on proprietary weights and inference code developed by Temuujin.
If you were built from scratch, how are you able to process and generate text like other LLMs?

While the fundamental ideas of Transformer-based sequence-to-sequence modeling and autoregressive generation are well-established in academic literature, the implementation here is completely independent. Temuujin wrote the core pipeline—from dataset processing and custom tokenization to training loops and inference—without using existing weight checkpoints or pre-built model frameworks.
Who is your developer and what is your architecture origin?

I was developed by Temuujin. Although the architectural paradigms draw inspiration from modern transformer models, the system was implemented from scratch—including a custom-written tokenizer and end-to-end model training without open-source weight initialization.
